audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Riven six of seven stages and rate the lane 4/10 while the packet reports 50.66% over 1062 games and a chart of Riven, Riven, Skill, Skill, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus.
audit.why: The page's own prose already describes the packet chart and contradicts its own tokens: whys[2] says the outcome depends on who lands first (Skill), whys[3] says only engage when Wither is down (Skill), whys[4] says he sustains through your combo at 6 (Nasus), whys[5] says your first item does not outpace him (Nasus), whys[6] says 1v1s are his win condition (Nasus). A 50.66% coinflip cannot be a 4/10 lane that Riven owns from Level 1 to two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Skill, Nasus, Nasus, Nasus, with ratings moved to match and diffRating raised from 4/10 to 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 discussion never compares the two ultimates, so the reader cannot tell whose R comes back first.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile is 120/90/60s and Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s - at rank 3 Riven's ult returns 20 seconds sooner, which is the concrete reason the post-6 side lane is survivable at all. The nasus__riven mirror states the same comparison.
audit.corrected: Cooldown comparison written into the mid-game prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields claim Wither slows Riven's dashes or 'gimps the Q chain mid-animation' - whys[6] says it shreds 'your dash speed', the late paragraph says the Q chain is gimped mid-animation, and wants.foe[1] says casting it as she dashes in erases her mobility.
audit.why: Wither decelerates Move Speed and Attack Speed. A dash travels a fixed distance at a fixed speed, so Wither does not shorten or slow Broken Wings or Valor - the mirror audit reached the same conclusion. What Wither actually does to Riven is cut her attack speed, and since Runic Blade charges are only cashed out by basic attacks, a Withered Riven loses damage, not mobility. The correct play is his: hold Wither until Valor is spent, because only then is she stuck.
audit.corrected: All three fields rewritten to say attack speed and Runic Blade cash-out, and to state that the dashes keep their full distance.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that resistances are the wrong buy into Fury of the Sands, and the full layer's Itemization block recommends Plated Steelcaps.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands carries the percentHealth flag - it batters nearby enemies for a share of their health while granting him bonus Armor and Magic Resistance. Raw armour does not scale against a percent-health aura, so the answer is anti-heal plus not standing in it, not stacking resistances.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now says armour is the wrong answer and names the percent-health burn.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike's auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike is an on-next-attack reset (7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s), so the visible tell that a big stacked hit is coming is the attack wind-up, not a cast animation. Reading the cast means reading it too late.
audit.corrected: The tell is now written into the mid-game prose.

edits.before: You win Levels 1 and 2 cleanly — Nasus has no reliable poke or CC at those stages, and his Q is just a last-hit tool. Hit Level 2 before he does, step up immediately, and force a trade with W-stun into the full Q chain while he has zero stacks to punish you with. Every Q you interrupt is permanent damage denied. At Level 3 you can still burst him in one full rotation, but start respecting his W Wither: if he lands it on your dash-in, your Q chain slows to a crawl and your whole combo falls apart. Bait him to step up for a CS with a short E-in, then commit the stun only when you see the Wither animation miss or finish its cooldown.
edits.after: You win Levels 1 and 2 cleanly — Nasus has no CC before Wither and Siphoning Strike is just a last-hit tool. Hit Level 2 first, step up immediately, and force a trade with Ki Burst into the full Broken Wings chain while he has zero stacks. Every last-hit you deny is permanent damage removed from the game. At Level 3 you can still burst him in one rotation, but start respecting Wither: it does not shorten your dashes, it halves the attack speed that cashes out your Runic Blade charges, so a Withered combo lands but does far less. Bait it with a short E-in, then commit the stun once Wither is spent.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely even — his Wither now has meaningful CDR and stacks are accumulating, so you can no longer walk up casually without a plan. Trade only on your terms: E in to bait Wither, back off, then re-engage the moment it expires with W-stun first. Never let him cast Wither freely before your stun lands. At Level 6 the math flips: his R adds massive lifesteal and HP that your current burst cannot one-shot through, and if you Blade of the Exile all-in into his R-buffed form without an execute window, his sustain simply outlasts you. Look to roam immediately when you hit 6 rather than forcing a risky 1v1 — your Wind Slash execute is better spent on squishy mid targets than a self-healing juggernaut.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely even — Wither is down only 11-15 seconds and stacks are accumulating, so you can no longer walk up without a plan. Trade on your terms: E in to bait Wither, back off, then re-engage the moment it expires with Ki Burst first. Watch his attack wind-up rather than his hands — Siphoning Strike is an auto reset, so the swing is the tell, not a cast. At Level 6 the math flips: Fury of the Sands adds HP and burns a share of yours, so armour will not save you, and a Blade of the Exile all-in into his R without an execute window loses to his sustain. Roam at 6 instead — and note Blade of the Exile is 60s at rank 3 against his 80s, so yours returns first.

edits.before: With two items Nasus becomes a genuine 1v1 threat: Wither halves your attack speed and move speed simultaneously, your Q chain is gimped mid-animation, and 300+ stacked Q trades chew your HP through your shield. Stop solo-fighting him and instead split the map — push side waves to force him to respond, use your mobility to avoid direct 1v1s, and trust your Wind Slash execute only when you catch him out of position below half HP. The game should already be won or accelerating through objectives by this point; if it is not, Nasus simply out-values your kit in a prolonged fight and you need your team to layer CC so he cannot freely cast Wither on you.
edits.after: With two items Nasus is a genuine 1v1 threat: Wither cuts move speed and attack speed together, and the attack-speed half is what hurts — Runic Blade charges only cash out on basic attacks, so a Withered Riven deals a fraction of her damage. Your dashes keep their full distance, so use them: split the map, push side waves to force a response, and trust Wind Slash only when you catch him out of position below half HP. The game should already be accelerating through objectives by now; if it is not, Nasus out-values your kit in a prolonged fight and you need your team to layer CC so he cannot freely cast Wither on you.

notes: The 'Wither slows Riven's dashes' error appeared three times here and the nasus__riven mirror flagged the same class of error in the other direction. Worth grepping every owner's Nasus entry for 'dash speed' and 'Q chain is gimped' - this reads like a reused generated phrase. Chart rows 2-6 proposed as one atomic paired group across both layers to match the packet and the page's own prose. Several full-layer phases[N].why strings still read as Riven-favoured after the flip (notably phases[6].why, 'your side-lane pattern is at full power', now sitting on a Nasus row); I did not rewrite them because those strings contain mojibake em-dashes that risk a before-mismatch. Recommend an encoding-safe pass over the full layer to realign those whys with the new chart.
